newsitem.title: USA: Dell stock soars, lifting other PC makers.
newsitem.headline: Dell stock soars, lifting other PC makers.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp. stock soared Wednesday after it reported sharply higher earnings, fuelling a rally in computer stocks as investors bet Dell's results pointed to strong profits for the industry.

Dell shares jumped $8 to $107.625 in heavy trading on Nasdaq. Dell said after the market closed on Tuesday that earnings more than doubled to $198 million, or $1.08 a share, in the latest quarter, exceeding analysts' average estimate of 93 cents a share.
The company's stock rose $2.125 on Tuesday as investors had bet on strong results.
Dell's earnings not only beat the average estimates on Wall Street but also beat the $1 to $1.05 a share that some traders had expected, the so-called whisper number, analysts said.
"What happens when a bellwether like Dell turns numbers in like this, people assume the demand climate is generally good," said Mark Specker, a SoundView Financial analyst.
"They are growing at about three times faster than the rest of the industry. It's blistering."

In its report, Dell said sales jumped 62 percent to $2.6 billion from $1.6 billion in the quarter ended on May 4. Sales jumped 64 percent in the Americas, 38 percent in Europe and 90 percent in the Asia-Pacific region, including Japan.
Specker noted that Dell's growth also was coming at the expense of competitors such as troubled PC maker AST Research Inc., whose stock was barely changed at $5.22 on Nasdaq.
Other PC shares jumped. Compaq Computer Corp. rose $6 to $103 on the New York Stock Exchange and Gateway 2000 Inc. added $3 to $74.125 on Nasdaq.
Gateway was also expected to unveil an aggressive plan to boost its corporate business later Wednesday.
Shares of Intel, whose chips are used in 80 percent of all PCs, rose $2.75 to $163.75 and software giant Microsoft Corp. added $2 to $121.125, both on Nasdaq.
International Business Machines Corp. rose $1.75 to $175.50 on the NYSE.
